fix.sql: ANALYZE TABLE `shop`.`orders` UPDATE HISTOGRAM ON `promo_code`, `created_at` WITH 64 BUCKETS;
fix.summary: Build a histogram for these columns. It reads the table once; MySQL doesn't refresh it on its own, so run it again after large data changes.

findings.summary: 2 of the heaviest queries filter orders on promo_code and created_at, which no index starts with and no histogram describes, so MySQL assumes a fixed share of rows match (10% for =, a third for ranges); EXPLAIN shows filtered = 10.00%, one of those guesses. When the real share is far off, common for status flags and skewed values, it picks the wrong join order or access path. A histogram costs nothing at query time and changes only when you run ANALYZE again.
findings.title: MySQL guesses how many orders rows match promo_code and created_at: no histogram
verify: Re-scan: the columns should have histograms, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE should show estimated rows close to actual for that filter.
